prs.title: feat(vite-server): describe the deploy target on the server build
prs.author: danielroe
prs.body: ### 🔗 Linked issue ### 📚 Description this pairs with nuxt/cli#1671, which reports the configured server builder instead of assuming Nitro. `nuxt build` prints the server builder's deploy target, but this was only populated by nitro, so this is a (small) start to doing the same for`@nuxt/vite-server`: | configuration | `target` | | --- | --- | | no deploy plugin | `node` | | `@cloudflare/vite-plugin` | `cloudflare` | | `@netlify/vite-plugin` with `build.enabled` | `netlify` | | `@netlify/vite-plugin` without it (dev emulation only) | `node` | | `vite-plugin-vercel` | `vercel` | | `@universal-deploy/vite` node adapter | `node` | | an unrecognised plugin that claims the `ssr` input | `undefined` | | `ssr: false`, or `nuxt generate` | `undefined` |

prs.title: fix(vite): keep absolute paths for externalised `shared/` imports
prs.author: danielroe
prs.body: ### 🔗 Linked issue ### 📚 Description currently, relative imports from `shared/` fail the production buil this is caused by rolldown's default `makeAbsoluteExternalsRelative: 'ifRelativeSource'`, which assumes that the output matches the input... this sets `makeAbsoluteExternalsRelative: false` for the ssr environment to keep them absolute, so nitro will continue to bundle them as it does for `#shared/`

prs.title: fix(nuxt,vite,webpack,rsbuild): resolve every vue import to a single copy
prs.author: danielroe
prs.body: ### 🔗 Linked issue ### 📚 Description spotted this while debugging an issue in nuxt-modules/storybook ecosystem-ci vit'es `resolve.dedupe` only works when `vue` resolves from the vite root, and it's possible for users to have projects where that's not the case, even though we have had it in the dependencies of the nuxt starter since 2023. so this PR resolves every bundled import of a vue runtime package (`vue`, `@vue/runtime-dom`, `@vue/runtime-core`, `@vue/reactivity`, `@vue/shared`, `@vue/server-renderer`, `@vue/runtime-vapor`) to the copy nuxt resolves, following vue's own dependency chain. this helps to avoid duplicate copies of vue, which can be common in a monorepo setup

prs.title: fix(nuxt,nitro)!: make vue and vue-router peer dependencies
prs.author: danielroe
prs.body: ### 🔗 Linked issue ### 📚 Description nuxt depends on `vue` and `vue-router` directly, but we also have it as a dependency in our starters since since nuxt/starter#525. as updates come in - and particularly in monorepos - it's easy for a project to end up with different versions of `vue` alongside nuxt's. 👉 so now we make them peer dependencies of `nuxt`. > [!NOTE] > `vue-router` is an optional peer dep as nuxt only imports it at runtime for `pages/`. new projects have listed both in `package.json` since 2023 so this shouldn't hit many people, but we also prompt to install both at startup if they aren't present, and check the version of vue against the constraints nuxt requires.

prs.title: fix(nuxt): sort payload keys for deterministic serialisation
prs.author: danielroe
prs.body: ### 🔗 Linked issue ### 📚 Description I noticed this when looking into ISR costs for npmx.dev: two consecutive regenerations of `/package/vue/_payload.json` had identical data but different bytes (15645 B vs 15683 B). this is because keys are added to the `payload` in the order async work settles, and devalue's output follows insertion order, so the same data serialises differently from one render to the next that means content-derived ETags don't match and isr writes or cdn caching miss more frequently, which can increase costs this PR sorts the keys of `data`, `state`, `once` and `_errors` when serialising the payload. (the perf cost here is within noise, and potential savings is much more significant.)

prs.title: perf(nuxt): do not key cached payload urls on the build id
prs.author: danielroe
prs.body: ### 🔗 Linked issue ### 📚 Description this came out of looking at ISR costs for npmx.dev. every distinct query string is potentially it's own cache/CDN entry, and we tag every payload URL with `?_b=`. after each deploy, every client still on the previous build ends up regenerating the payload. in fact, `_b` can't do anything useful for cached (`isr`/`swr`/`cache`) routes, because the payload is mutable within a deploy, the server already strips it, and the payload now carries its own `buildId`, which we check with `isOutdatedPayload`. so this stops adding the build id as `_b` to payload URLs for cached routes, on both the client and the server-rendered preload link.

prs.title: fix(nuxt): resolve never-hydrated chunks from precomputed renderer deps
prs.author: danielroe
prs.body: ### 🔗 Linked issue follow-up to #35812 ### 📚 Description in production builds, the JS chunk for a `hydrate-never` component is still emitted as a resource hint and fetched eagerly, even though the client can never hydrate it, because `rendererContext.manifest` isn't present after #33361 this change falls back to `rendererContext.precomputed.modules` when there is no manifest

prs.title: fix(nuxt): parse and serialise queries the same way the router does
prs.author: danielroe
prs.body: ### 📚 Description a few places in nuxt parse or build query strings with `ufo` rather than the router, so the result differs from vue-router: ```ts // in route middleware return navigateTo('/search?flag', { replace: true }) // lands on `/search?flag=` navigateTo({ path: 'https://example.com/search', query: { q: '', path: 'a/b' } }, { external: true }) // goes to `https://example.com/search?q&path=a%2Fb`, rather than `?q=&path=a/b` ``` the same goes for `` with an object `to` pointing at an external url, and for `route.query` in the custom slot of an external `` (`?flag` gives `''` rather than `null`). this PR exposes `parseQuery` and `stringifyQuery` from `#build/pages`, so we can use whatever the router uses: vue-router's (or any overrides from `router.options`) with `pages/`, and `ufo` otherwise cc: @posva

prs.title: feat(nuxt,vite-server): add `render:document` hook
prs.author: danielroe
prs.body:
### 🔗 Linked issue follows up #36601, https://github.com/nuxt/nuxt/issues/36571 ### 📚 Description I've been porting `@nuxtjs/critters` to Nuxt 5, and it needs the finished HTML document: it scans the whole page for used selectors and then rewrites the head and stylesheet links. on Nuxt 4 it used `render:response`, which runs after every `render:html` listener. on Nuxt 5 the only portable hook is `render:html`, and since listeners run in registration order, anything added by a later listener (including every `server/plugins/` file in the app itself) never reaches it. this adds a `render:document` renderer hook. it can be registered from a renderer plugin or with `useServerHooks()`, so it works under any server builder. | response | `render:document` | | --- | --- | | buffered page, error page, `ssr: false` route | called | | streamed | not called (there's no complete document) | | server component | not called | | `@nuxt/vite-server` static SPA document | called after `render:html`: once per build, or for each navigation in dev | in the renderer, the document is only serialised when a listener reads `html`, so unless one replaces it the response keeps the chunk-by-chunk encoding from #36719.

& …(truncated)

prs.title: feat(nuxt): catch server-side errors in `<NuxtErrorBoundary>`
prs.author: danielroe
prs.body: ### 🔗 Linked issue resolves #25445 relates to #15781 (solves the SSR half; the other needs #35642) ### 📚 Description `` previously just caught client-side errors, so a component that throws during SSR goes straight past it to `error.vue`. this PR makes it work on the server too: ```vue ``` if `` throws on the server, the response is a `200` with the rest of the page intact and `#error` in its place, and the client hydrates it in the same state (ie with error fallback). errors created with `createError` (or any other HTTP error) keep their `status` and `data`, but in production anything else reaches the slot as a bare `500` so server error messages stay out of the HTML. it's behind `experimental.ssrErrorBoundary`, on by default for `compatibilityVersion: 5` `retry-on-client` re-renders the default slot once mounted, which is what `` does, so we now deprecate that as a separate component. both now share the same SSR buffer helper, which also fixes the client fallback not waiting for nested async components. cc: @huang-julien

prs.title: fix(nuxt): render `<ClientOnly>` fallback slots from vapor components
prs.author: danielroe
prs.body:
### 📚 Description

with the latest vue 3.6 RC, a `<ClientOnly>` with a `#fallback` slot inside a vapor component fails to SSR:

```
TypeError: _push is not a function
```

this is because the server renderer wraps slots passed from a vapor component as a function that takes two args, but `<ClientOnly>` renders its fallback with `h`, which treats the slot as a functional component...

this renders the fallback through a small functional component that calls the slot with `{}` instead, so it's still its own component vnode (as in #30664) but the slot only receives slot props.

prs.title: perf(nuxt): avoid `navigateTo` in the client pages-less router
prs.author: danielroe
prs.body: ### 📚 Description the pages-less router corrects the initial URL with `navigateTo`, which pulls `navigateTo` and its URL helpers into every app without pages, even ones that never call it. so, on the client we now directly call `routerPush`, which is what `navigateTo` ends up calling there anyway. the server still uses `navigateTo` for redirects... it also fixes the `@__NO_SIDE_EFFECTS__` annotations in `nuxt.ts` that rolldown ignores, which silences the `INVALID_ANNOTATION` warning the minimal fixtures print on every build... 😆

prs.title: fix(nuxt): emit lossless rou3 patterns for `ssrRoutes`
prs.author: danielroe
prs.body: ### 🔗 Linked issue https://github.com/nitrojs/nitro-v2/pull/41 ### 📚 Description checking npmx, a lot of the requests are misattributed to the `/__fallback` function, because we strip `ssrRoutes` of every `(...)` and `?` this PR builds `ssrRoutes` with `vueRouterToRou3` instead, without collapsing or expanding, so params keep their names and each page path still gives one pattern: | page path | before | after | | --- | --- | --- | | `/package-code/:org?/:name/v/:version/:filePath(.*)?` | `/package-code/:org/:name/v/:version/:filePath` | `/package-code/:org?/:name/v/:version/:filePath(.*)` | | `/x/:id?` | `/x/:id` | `/x/:id?` | | `/:slug(.*)*` | `/**:slug` | `/:slug(.*)` |

prs.title: fix(nuxt): encode middleware redirect query like vue-router on server
prs.author: danielroe
prs.body:
### 🔗 Linked issue

follow-up to https://github.com/nuxt/nuxt/pull/36112

### 📚 Description

since 4.6, a server-side `navigateTo` from route middleware changes the `Location` of every redirect whose query is percent-encoded. for example:

```ts
return navigateTo(withQuery('/login', { redirect: to.path }))
```

4.5 sent `Location: /login?redirect=/protected` and 4.6 sends `Location: /login?redirect=%2Fprotected`. this broke redirect assertions in `@nuxtjs/hanko`, and probably in other modules too.

this was an unintended side effect of #36112, so this instead builds `Location` from the already-resolved normalised path

prs.title: fix(vite): track client and SSR entries separately for inline styles
prs.author: danielroe
prs.body: ### 📚 Description when `features.inlineStyles` is enabled and a module rewires only the client entry (for example `nuxt-booster` swapping the client `input.entry` for a wrapper), the server-rendered html has no global CSS at all this PR tracks the client and SSR entries separately, and treats the client entry as the source of entry-level CSS when extracting styles on the server.

prs.title: fix(nuxt): don't use static data for watch-triggered refresh
prs.author: danielroe
prs.body: ### 📚 Description previously, once a key was in `nuxtApp.static.data`, changing a `watch` source didn't refetch. this is because `getDefaultCachedData` skipped `static.data` for `refresh:manual` and `refresh:hook` but not for `watch` this reads `static.data` only for the initial resolution, so a watch behaves like a manual `refresh()`.

prs.title: fix(nuxt): settle asyncData promise when request is aborted externally
prs.author: danielroe
prs.body:
### 📚 Description

`execute` and `refresh` never settle when the request is aborted by a signal the caller passed in:

```ts
const controller = new AbortController()
const promise = execute({ signal: controller.signal })
controller.abort()
await promise // never resolves, and a later `execute({ dedupe: 'defer' })` waits on it forever
```

so this returns nothing from those branches instead, as we already do on success
